body:
Metricool: scheduled Sun 2026-10-25 13:00 IG + TikTok
2 Vercel settings before your bill grows: drop Turbo builds, add an Ignored Build Step. CTA: VERCEL.
guide: Cut the build minutes Vercel bills you for by changing two project settings. You need a Vercel project connected to a Git repository.
1. Open your project in the Vercel dashboard and go to Settings, then the build and deployment section.
1. Check which build machine the project uses, and switch off the Turbo (faster, higher-priced) build machine if you don't need it.
1. Rebuild once on the standard machine and compare the build time and cost with the Turbo run before you decide to keep it off.
1. In the Git settings, find the Ignored Build Step and set a command that tells Vercel when to skip a build.
1. Make that command skip builds when nothing the site uses has changed, for example only a README or notes file.
1. Push a change that should be skipped and one that shouldn't, and check in the Deployments tab that the first is cancelled and the second builds.
1. Look at your usage and billing page after a few days to confirm the build minutes are falling.
Watch out: an Ignored Build Step that is too broad will skip builds you need, so test it on both kinds of change before you rely on it.

```
You are helping me reduce my Vercel build costs. I have a Vercel project called <project name> connected to a <GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket> repository, and my app is built with <framework, e.g. Next.js>. I am not an expert, so explain each step in plain English.
Do three things:
1. Tell me exactly where in the Vercel dashboard to check which build machine my project uses, and how to switch from a Turbo build machine to the standard one.
2. Write an Ignored Build Step command for my repository that skips a deployment when the only files changed are <files or folders that don't affect the site, e.g. docs, README, notes>. Explain how Vercel reads the command's exit code, and where in the project settings I paste it.
3. Give me a short test plan: one change that should be skipped, one that should build, and what I should see in the Deployments tab for each.
Constraints: use only standard Vercel settings, don't change my application code, and warn me of any case where the command could skip a build I need. Return the command in one code block, then the numbered steps.
```
I wrote this from the post's two settings only. I haven't checked the current Vercel dashboard wording for the build machine setting, so the menu names may differ slightly.
